trial_court: Family Court, Camp at Bahadurgarh, HMA/53/2023
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Parties solemnized marriage in 2005. Two children born out of wedlock. Petitioner seeking transfer of petition filed by respondent under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.

legal_principles.principle: Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
legal_principles.held: Transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to consider the economic soundness of both parties.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.

legal_principles.principle: The Courts should consider the convenience of the wife in matrimonial disputes.
legal_principles.held: Given the prevailing socioeconomic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.

outcome.final_order: Transfer of petition to a court of competent jurisdiction at Bhiwani ordered.
